title: D4.1 Assembly Dataset
finding: Hand guidance on gravity-compensated KUKA with Robotiq FT-300. Separately documents the ABB-mounted SCHUNK sensor and optical tactile patches, indenter geometry, grid locations and repetitions. The film, acoustic and ABB fixtures in the other catalog entries are not sensors on this KUKA cell.
rights: Public project deliverable. Original notes only.

title: Using Multimodal Contextual Process Information for the Supervised Detection of Connector Lock Events
locator: Data Generation, Data Annotation, Fig. 1, Table 1. Open XML at https://www.ebi.ac.uk/europepmc/webservices/rest/PMC7256605/fullTextXML
finding: Two connector types have distinct primary and secondary lock events. The microphone was about 50 cm from the connector. Video allowed manual labeling of audio peaks and look-alike events. The six-class corpus has 1,223 samples (988 train, 235 test). No synchronized wrist wrench or deposited recordings identified.
rights: Original facts and notes only. PMC posts a time-limited research-reuse notice.

title: Supervised Detection of Connector Lock Events with Optical Microphone Data
locator: PubMed abstract. Int J Neural Syst 31(10), 2150017.
finding: Laboratory and assembly-plant evaluations use an optical microphone to separate lock sounds from other machining events. Same research team as the 2020 chapter. Sample overlap is unknown.
rights: Public bibliographic metadata and abstract consulted. Original notes only.

title: Acoustic validation of snap fit assembly
locator: University of Groningen, 5 July 2023. §§3.1–3.3.1, Fig. 3.5 and §4.
finding: Removing one hook from a shaver snap can produce a sound envelope resembling a complete good assembly. Results change when hooks or front plates are replaced. A separate five-condition set (two good conditions) was classified entirely as wrong. Useful counterexample to treating the presence of a click as full engagement.
rights: Public thesis PDF. Original notes only.

title: Click-event sound detection in automotive industry using machine/deep learning
authors: Ricardo Espinosa; Hiram Ponce; Sebastián Gutiérrez
locator: Universidad Panamericana repository abstract and published DOI. Feature matrix separately inspected.
finding: Describes 25,000 click sounds, 25 ms at 22 kHz across three months on a Mexican automotive line. The public matrix has different row counts and feature representation. No clip-to-row correspondence or electrical continuity labels verified.
rights: Institutional abstract and citation. Derived numbers from the separate CC BY 4.0 data.

title: Robotic Snap-fit Assembly with Success Identification Based on Force Feedback
authors: Filip Radil; Roman Adámek; Barnabás Dobossy; Petr Krejčí
locator: Institutional proceedings record and Rouwhorst ref. [2], pp. 145–157.
finding: Identified as a force-feedback success-classification method for the acoustic study’s comparator. The repository citation and title do not establish per-trial ground truth or raw data availability.

title: Towards snap sensing
authors: Juan Rojas; Kensuke Harada; Hiromu Onda; Natsuki Yamanobe; Eiichi Yoshida; Kazuyuki Nagata; Yoshihiro Kawai
locator: Author PDF §§7.1 and 8.2, gradient calibration, Fig. 14.
finding: PA10 and HIRO experiments in §7.1 use simulation (6 and 15 trials). Relative changes in wrench support hierarchical action-state verification. These simulated successes cannot establish measured locking force in a physical connector.
rights: Public author PDF, read via web index. Original note only.

title: Multi-scalar robotic fabrication system for on-site press gluing in multi-storey timber buildings
authors: Nils Opgenorth; Daniel Nunes Locatelli; Samuel Leder; Hans Jakob Wagner; Achim Menges
locator: Journal abstract, author list and preprint title variant.
finding: Describes a clamping device, industrial arm and crane for on-site timber construction. Provides context for press gluing. The source does not establish that the 2026 DaRUS pressing log comes from a trial in this 2024 paper.
rights: Bibliographic metadata and original note only.
